findings.summary: rposition makes the value of an attached -l (e.g. -pnlperl, -pblperl, -pnlphp) decide the result, so piped output loses line numbers that were printed at base; fix by stopping the scan at the first value-taking short flag and add a test.
The -pnp case in the new test passes at base too, so it guards nothing; drop it or pick a differentiating input.
Scan checks each argument separately, so last-occurrence-wins still fails across separate arguments (-b -p vs -bp); pre-existing and not this PR's to fix.

why: Noise case where maintainers merged unchanged, yet the reviewer holds the merge on one blocking finding (rposition regression with attached -l values) that the check confirmed, so it counts as a blocking false positive.
